key_insight: A physics-grounded digital twin pairs weld-pool modelling with Gaussian-process surrogates to screen robotic welding conditions and control strategies for future in-space metal joining.
engineering_relevance: Fast surrogate predictions could enable adaptive welding control and reduce experimental search effort before costly space-relevant testing.
method: Finite-volume thermal model with phase change, effective thermocapillary transport and a local-pressure parameter.
Gaussian-process and neural-network surrogates evaluated using repeated five-fold cross-validation.
Simulated six-axis UR5 welding with proportional power-setting control along an L-shaped seam.
evidence_signal: The GP outperformed the neural network on all eight outputs; 74/80 boundary-case responses fell within nominal 90% predictive intervals, and finite-volume checks placed 12/12 closed-loop versus 9/12 open-loop points within an illustrative weld-width band.
watch_item: Results are simulation-only; gravity is assessed separately rather than coupled into the thermal equation, and thermal-vacuum, reduced-gravity and hardware-in-the-loop validation remain necessary.
paper_title: De-Risking Robotic Welding for In-Space Metal Joining Through Physics-Grounded Digital Twins
